title: Cloud Metadata Credential Theft
overview: Find a network classification showing an unexpected workload requesting the cloud metadata credential service.
prerequisites: Know the basics of Cloud auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Cloud Instance Metadata API
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A metadata credential request by an unapproved workload warrants checking workload identity and access policy.
evidence: Read the caller classification and verdict, then pivot to cloud audit for any follow-on role activity.
false_positive: A deployed agent or SDK may require metadata access to obtain authorized role credentials.
tuning: Map approved workloads and separate credential requests from benign metadata classes.
response: Preserve application and network records, scope workload identity and remove unauthorized permission or access.
prevention: Require IMDSv2 where supported, constrain metadata access and limit instance-role privileges.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fixture uses a classification. It sends no metadata requests and includes neither credential values nor live target addresses.

questions.prompt: Which context matters beyond metadata access?
options: What was requested and which workload made the request
questions.explanation: Authorized agents make some requests. Caller and request type add context.

questions.prompt: Which source helps determine if a role was used afterward?
questions.explanation: Cloud audit can show subsequent API activity by the role.
